summary:
Twenty-six messages, 16 from Vale and 10 from ALTR — and nine of those ten came from one person who had never really worked this account before. This was the week the named team disappeared and was replaced by a single emergency. Ollie Mckinlay, the account lead, sent ZERO messages (last seen Sep 15, ten days). Stephski sent zero (nine days). Mica Vecco sent zero (eight days). Michelle sent zero, and her weekly leak-removal breakdown — the one service on this account that has never failed in five months — has now missed two consecutive cycles and is 17 days overdue, so the watch item raised last week converts into a live complaint exactly as the carry-forward file instructed. Derrek is 55 days silent. What did happen is serious in both directions. Vale's main Instagram, @valebragg, has been restricted: she posted a screenshot on Sep 22, and Vivek — her Meta Support Rep since Jul 29, whose entire prior output in this chat was the single word '@ofwizz' on Aug 3 — answered in eleven minutes with 'Username ma'am', worked it over three days, removed an offending link on Sep 23, and reported on Sep 25 that the account is 'in review'. That is real, responsive service and the first of it he has ever given her. It is also how ALTR asked a client to hand over a live password in a group chat. Vivek wrote 'Share password' (Sep 22). Vale posted '@valebragg

[REDACTED-PASSWORD]' (Sep 23), was told 'Password is wrong', posted '[REDACTED-PASSWORD]', was told 'Still wrong', then wrote 'Okay let me change it' and posted her newly-set live credential, '[REDACTED-PASSWORD]', in plain text into a Telegram group whose membership includes two people silently added on Sep 10 and Sep 17 with no introduction. That password is still sitting in the chat, unrotated, nine days after Mica's own Sep 17 broadcast told her 'Please do not send your backup codes to anyone, including our team' — and 59 days after Vale asked 'Should I change my password?' (Jul 28) and was never answered. The exposed handle is the same one she told the DMCA team gets the most leaks 'since it’s my instagram name'. Everything else aged another seven days without a word from anyone. The paid-but-undelivered fan money went a SIXTH consecutive window unmentioned: John's $2,000 custom plus the $200 ASAP fee, delivered by Vale on Aug 22, is 34 days unconfirmed; the March-to-date reconciliation is 38 days unstarted; Ryan's $600 videocall is 111 days from sale, John's $1,800 videocall 147 days, Tyler's $700 JOI custom 173 days. Three consecutive client payments remain unreconciled — Aug 17 (39 days), Sep 5 (20) and Sep 16 (9) — against a bank account ALTR changed twice in that span and an invoice that itself raised 'bounce backs' ten days ago; Stephski has not spoken since. The written account rulebook is 44 days old, the girl-girl vault purge 54, the sexting-set template 59. And the four uncaptioned photos Vale posted into the OnlyFans topic on Sep 17 and Sep 18 — almost certainly the Lost Lands festival content she promised on Sep 15 'so that the fans feel like they’re there with me' — have still never drawn a single reply from anybody, eight days on. The quietest new signal is the one to watch hardest: on Sep 22 Mayson wrote 'Hey @valebragg05 let me know when you’re available for our call!' and Vale did not answer. She was in the chat eight hours later posting her Instagram screenshot. In six months she has never once left a call request unanswered — she replied same-day on Jun 8, Jun 29 and Jul 13. The biweekly cadence is now 74 days dead, and for the first time the client is the one not replying.

health.rationale: Down 7 from 45, the sharpest fall since Aug 28, and it is deserved. FOUR of the five named people on this account sent nothing at all this week: Ollie Mckinlay (10 days silent, and the account lead has now closed nothing in six consecutive reports), Stephski (9 days, with three of the client's payments still unreconciled and her own 'bounce backs' line 10 days unexplained), Mica Vecco (8 days, hook test 25 days unread-out) and Michelle — whose weekly leak-removal breakdown has now missed TWO cycles and stands at 17 days against a five-month maximum gap of nine. Last week's file said in terms: re-open the leak-monitoring complaint if Sep 22 passes with no report. It passed. The single reliable service on this account has stopped, and nobody has said a word about it. Against that, one genuine and overdue win: Vivek finally did the job he was introduced for on Jul 29. He answered Vale's Instagram restriction screenshot in eleven minutes, stayed with it across three days and got the offending link removed — nine of ALTR's ten messages this week were his. But the way he did it created the worst new item on the account: he asked a client to 'Share password' in a group chat, and she posted three of them in plain text, ending with the live credential she had just reset. It is still there, unrotated, in a chat that gained two unintroduced members on Sep 10 and Sep 17, five days before the password landed. ALTR's own social lead had broadcast 'Please do not send your backup codes to anyone, including our team' five days earlier, and the client's own Jul 28 question 'Should I change my password?' has gone 59 days unanswered. Meanwhile her main Instagram — the top of her entire OnlyFans funnel, already collapsed from 200k+ reach to under 3k for 25 days — is now formally under review with no outcome. Nothing else moved: sixth silent window on roughly $5,300 of paid-but-undelivered fan money (34/111/147/173 days), 38 days with the reconciliation unstarted, 44 days with no written account rulebook after the client disclosed a chatter's error once cost her nine days of account access, 54 days on the girl-girl vault purge, 59 on the sexting template and the Infloww security enquiry. Four photos she posted on Sep 17-18, almost certainly the festival content she volunteered, were never acknowledged. And the client did not answer a direct call request for the first time in six months. Prior scores: 70 (Aug 8), 62 (Aug 14), 60 (Aug 21), 48 (Aug 28), 52 (Sep 4, unpublished), 47 (Sep 11), 45 (Sep 18).
